2019_38.concept: $\chi^2_m$ is the sum of $m$ squared standard normals. More degrees of freedom gives a stochastically larger variable.
2019_38.solution: If $m>n$, write $X\overset d=Y+W$ with $W\sim\chi^2_{m-n}\ge0$ independent of $Y$. Then $P(X>a)\ge P(Y>a)$ for all $a$. So (b).
2019_38.shortcut: Adding a non-negative independent piece can only increase tail probabilities.

2019_59.concept: $\phi_X(t)=E(e^{itX})$. $|\phi(t)|=1$ at $t\ne0$ means the distribution sits on a lattice.
2019_59.solution: $\phi_X(2\pi)=E[\cos2\pi X]+iE[\sin2\pi X]=1$ gives $E[1-\cos2\pi X]=0$. Since $1-\cos2\pi X\ge0$, it must be 0 a.s., so $\cos2\pi X=1$, i.e. $X\in\mathbb Z$ a.s. Hence $P(X\in\mathbb Z)=1$.

2019_64.concept: By exchangeability, $E\left(\frac{X_i^2}{\sum X_j^2}\right)$ is the same for every $i$, and these 10 expectations sum to $E(1)=1$.
2019_64.solution:
Each equals $\frac1{10}=0.1$. The variance value 2 is irrelevant.
Alternative: $\frac{X_1^2}{\sum X_j^2}\sim\text{Beta}\left(\frac12,\frac92\right)$ with mean $\frac{1/2}{5}=0.1$.

2020_64.concept: The joint density of the order statistics of $n$ i.i.d. variables from $g$ is $n!\prod g(x_i)$ on $x_1<\dots<x_n$.
2020_64.solution:
1. $\frac{81}{4}x_1^2x_2^2x_3^2=3!\left(\frac32x_1^2\right)\left(\frac32x_2^2\right)\left(\frac32x_3^2\right)$, the order statistics of i.i.d. $g(x)=\frac32x^2$ on $[-1,1]$.
2. $X_1+X_2+X_3$ equals the sum of the unordered i.i.d. sample.
3. $EX=0$ and $EX^2=\int_{-1}^1\frac32x^4dx=\frac35$, so $\operatorname{Var}=3\times\frac35=1.8$.
2020_64.shortcut: Sums and symmetric functions of order statistics equal those of the original sample, so ordering doesn't matter.

2021_26.concept: The jumps of $F$ are the probabilities. Use $P(X\le1)$ and $EX$ to find the constants.
2021_26.solution:
1. $P(X\le1)=\frac a2=\frac12$, so $a=1$ and $P(X=1)=\frac12$.
2. $P(X=2)=\frac c6-\frac12$, $P(X=3)=1-\frac c6$.
3. $EX=\frac12+2\left(\frac c6-\frac12\right)+3\left(1-\frac c6\right)=\frac52-\frac c6=\frac53$, so $c=5$.
4. $A=\bigcup[1+\frac1n,3-\frac1n]=(1,3)$, an open interval. $P(X\in A)=P(X=2)=\frac13\approx0.33$.
2021_26.trap: The union of closed intervals here is **open**. 1 and 3 are never included.
